from.place: Native cohomological decomposition of smooth dualizing purity: concentration

title: Concentration of the native smooth exceptional constant object
statement: Let k₀ be a finite field and ℓ a prime different from its characteristic. Let a₀ : X₀ → Spec k₀ be separated, finite type, and smooth of relative dimension d ∈ ℕ. Use the native bounded constructible derived category of pro-etale Weil sheaves [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], not fixed pairs of derived objects. For any right adjoint J of the native derived compact-support functor Ra₀! and its adjunction adj, put K = J(ℚ̄_ℓ,Spec k₀[0]), with the canonical constant Weil structure [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]. Then K lies both in D≥−2d and D≤−2d for the canonical t-structure of the ambient derived category of pro-etale Weil sheaves. There is no assertion identifying its surviving cohomology sheaf. The geometric hypotheses use [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

proof.text: Base change a₀ to the algebraic closure. Separated finite type and smooth relative dimension d persist. Apply the counit-normalized native exceptional forgetting comparison to adj at the constant point object. Its scalar-unit normalization identifies the result with the ordinary common-stage exceptional constant object, including closure transport.

proof.text: Apply the smooth dualizing specialization of the coefficient-stage purity theorem. Its finite normalized trace is transported by integral reconstruction, rationalization, and common-stage descent exactly as in unit sk-thm-purity-transport. The resulting ordinary object is the constant Tate line shifted by 2d.

proof.text: The realized object has zero cohomology in degrees different from −2d. Forgetting the native Weil structure is induced by an exact conservative functor of abelian categories, and the section-module and closure-change realizations are exact equivalences on the indicated sheaves. They commute with cohomology and detect zero objects. Thus native cohomology also vanishes outside −2d. The canonical derived t-structure characterizes these vanishings as IsGE (−2d) and IsLE (−2d). No Frobenius identification of the surviving sheaf is used.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_dualizing_concentration (J : WeilComplex k₀ l (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)) ⥤ WeilComplex k₀ l X) (adj : derivedLowerShriek k₀ l (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)) ⊣ J) (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] : ((J.obj (WeilSheaf.toComplex.obj (WeilSheaf.adicConstant k₀ l (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))))).obj.IsGE (-2 * (d : ℤ))) ∧ ((J.obj (WeilSheaf.toComplex.obj (WeilSheaf.adicConstant k₀ l (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))))).obj.IsLE (-2 * (d : ℤ)))
